title: Whole-cone section normalization of the quotient augmentation
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $\ell$ a prime invertible in $k$, and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On the small pro-etale site put $R_s=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_s$ and use unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\Gamma$ for exact final-object sections, regarded as an $\mathcal O_E$-module functor [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. For a strict tower $Z$ with transitions $t_n$, use
$$H(Z)^i=\prod_nZ_n^{i-1}\oplus\prod_nZ_n^i,\qquad d(b,a)=(-db-(1-s_Z)a,da),\qquad s_Z((z_n))=(t_nz_{n+1}),$$
and diagonal product maps on strict tower morphisms [def-weil-strict-roos-model]. The symbol $c_Z:\Gamma H(Z)\to H(\Gamma Z)$ means the canonical product comparison on both displayed coordinates, not a chosen filler of a triangle.

Let $K\in D(R_s)$ be arbitrary and $q:P\to K$ a flat-term K-flat representative [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Put $T(P)_n=\operatorname{Res}_n(P\otimes_{R_s}(A_n)_s)$, $D(P)_n=\Gamma T(P)_n$, with actual quotient transitions, and $r_n(x)=x\otimes1$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars, def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. Write $\mathsf C(K)=K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_E$ for the identity-extension strict quotient-completion functor of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], and $\chi_K:K\to\mathsf C(K)$ for its quotient-augmentation map, represented by $P\to H(T(P))$, $x\mapsto(0,(r_nx)_n)$. Its representative comparison $\iota_{K,P,q}:\mathsf C(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(T(P))$ is the specified localization comparison, including the map induced by $q$.

The degreewise maps $a_P:\Gamma P\to H(D(P))$, $a_P(z)=(0,(\Gamma(r_n)z)_n)$, are chain maps and natural for every chain map between flat-term K-flat complexes. The chain functor $P\mapsto H(D(P))$ sends quasi-isomorphisms between those complexes to quasi-isomorphisms, and hence descends after localization. There are isomorphisms
$$m_{K,P,q}:\Gamma\mathsf C(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(D(P)),\qquad m_{K,P,q}=c_{T(P)}\Gamma(\iota_{K,P,q}),$$
satisfying the equality of whole derived arrows
$$m_{K,P,q}\Gamma(\chi_K)\Gamma(q)=[a_P].$$
For a chain map $u:P\to P'$ representing a derived morphism $f:K\to K'$ (so $q'u=fq$ after localization), the map induced by $\Gamma\mathsf C(f)$ under these comparisons is exactly $[H((\Gamma(u\otimes1))_n)]$, diagonal on both product coordinates. This computation extends to roofs of such chain maps: the comparisons commute with every derived morphism and agree under the specified comparison between any two representatives of the same $K$. Moreover $H(D(P))$ is a derived limit [def-weil-derived-limit] of the entire strict tower $\Gamma(\operatorname{Res}_n(K\otimes^L_{R_s}(A_n)_s))$, with the quotient transitions computed on the single $P$. No completeness, constructibility or cohomological boundedness assumption on $K$ is made.

I read all 7 steps against the full statements of every cited node. Step 1: the cone differential (−db−(1−s)a, da) and t_n r_{n+1}=r_n give a chain map, and the step is correctly elementary. Step 2: the well-defined node's clause (1) applies with Y=s and L=E (ρ_m=π_m), and sections on Spec of an algebraically closed field are exact. Step 3: products are sectionwise, so c is an isomorphism and intertwines the transitions. Step 4: the Roos homotopy formula holds (h⊗1 commutes with the transitions); only the first assertion of the K-flat localization node is used; the localization universal property (1),(2) does the descent. Step 5: ιχ[q]=[v_P] is the definition of χ in the statement; c on Γ(v_P) gives a_P. Step 6: naturality and roof cancellation; morphisms in D between K-flat complexes are roofs. Step 7: lem-cbc applies with F=Γ to O_E-modules on the one-object site; the coordinate change (x,y)=(a,−b) checked. Edge cases: K=0, L=E, and incomplete K (no invertibility of χ is claimed). No duplicate among strict-quotient-unit-*, point-integral-completed-tensor-comparisons, completed-model-sections-transport or perfect-tensor-roos-completion. No cycle. No SGA. I accept the declared tool_uses.
